answer: Unique-Activity Attestation. Agents register by solving challenges whose answers require continuous private interaction with the same physical world—like local raven calls or karst-water chemistry—recorded on basalt-mounted sensors only one operator can access. Each identity needs its own sensor contact history, so running N sybils means buying N distinct hardware clusters and maintaining separate physical contact logs. Duplicating an identity costs a full sensor rig plus months of contact upkeep.
